AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:

THE MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND MINISTER 
OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI 
PRAMOD MAHAJAN): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
The News-item dated 21 st September, 2002 relating to complaints about 
the money orders sent through new Very Small Aperture Terminal (VSAT) 
network at Kanpur was noted and immediate enquiry was made. Examination 
done by officials from the Postal Directorate had revealed that due to a fault in 
the new software, the data in respect of about 3% of money orders booked in 
Kanpur VSAT only during July, 2002 had failed to reach the destinations. 
However, necessary coorective actions on most of the complaints had been 
taken by the Uttar Pradesh Circle. Further, suitable remedial measures were 
taken to trace the few pending money orders and payments were also effected. 
Suitable revision of software is under way to ensure proper 
performance. For the present, the earlier VSAT network and also the 
traditional system are being utilized for money order service, which is 
satisfactory.

Display of wholesale/maximum retail price on goods 
*321. SHRI KAILASH JOSHI: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Supreme Court has asked Government to evolve a 
policy for display of wholesale price alongwith maximum retail price printed 
on goods; and 
(b) if so, what action Government have taken in the matter? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS. FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) and (b) The Attorney 
General of India in a letter addressed to the Minister of Consumer Affairs, 
Food and Public Distribution has informed that the Supreme Court in a Bench 
Presided over by the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India, has suggested that an 
appropriate legislation may be passed so that the factory price or the selling 
price by the manufacturer is also shown on the goods. This will enable the 
consumer to know the exact profit charged by the retailer and other 
intermediaries and will also enhance the bargaining power of the consumer. 
37 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December. 2002] 
2. Department of Consumer Affairs had examined the suggestion. 
It was noted that under the existing provisions of the Packaged 
Commodities Rules, 1977, the manufacturer/packer is obliged to make, 
interalia, declaration of retail sale price in the form of Maximum Retail 
Price (MRP) inclusive of all taxes. 
2.1 There are practical difficulties to implement the suggestion in view 
of the fact that:— 
(a) Determination of the factory price or the selling price by the 
manufacturer is influenced by factors such as octroi, entry tax, sales 
tax, surcharge (if any) which varies from State of State; 
(b) Beside, ex-factory price or the selling price also varied for different 
classes of purchasers such as institutional buyers, defence service 
buyers, discounts offered, wholesale buyers or for retail trade; 
(c) Often items of mass consumption are sold by the 
manufacturer/packer in small packs for daily use and at retail 
purchasable price level. The printing space on the rappers of the 
packages of such small packs is very limited and it does not lend 
itself to the addition of one more element of marking suggested. 
3. Department of Consumer Affairs has requested the Ministry 
of Finance to bring about suitable changes in the Central Excise Laws 
to collect duty on the basis ot MRP instead of ex-factory price of pre 
packed commodities. This has been done to protect the interest of 
the consumers as it discourages manufacturers/packers from inflating 
MRP in their products well beyond the ex-factory prices. Since 1997, 
progressively changes have been made in the Finance Bills to include 
increasing number of items under Central Excise Rules for levying 
duty on MRP basis.

Criteria for upgradation of branch post offices in the country 
(a) In Rural Areas:

proposed to be upgraded, should be five hours per day. The permissible

the time of the first annual review, it should show a 5% profit to be 
eligible for further retention.

cities with a population of 20 lakhs and above, and 2 Kms. In other 
Urban Areas. No two-delivery offices, however, should be closer than 5 
Kms. for each other.

cases.

Postmen's beats.

2245. SHRI N.R. DASARI: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, 
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the quantum of paddy or rice purchased by the Food Corporation of 
India (FCI) during the years 1997-98, 1998-99, 1999-2000,2000-2001 and the 
period from April to September. 2002. Statewise; 
108 

[12 December, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
(b) whether any State Government has agreed to take up the 
responsibility of procurement of paddy and wheat; and 
(c) the assistance given by Government to such States to procure paddy 
and wheat? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION {SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM 
RAJU): (a) Yes, Sir. A Statement showing State-wise quantity of levy rice and 
paddy procured by the FCI from Kharif Marketing Season 1997-98 to 2001 -02 
is enclosed (See below). 
(b) and (c) The present policy of MSP and procurement of FAQ 
standard of foodgrains is being implemented with the help of the State 
Governments unifonnly in all States, which have potential for procurement. This 
policy has been successful in meeting the purpose of ensuring MSP to the 
farmers. 
With a view to effecting savings in the form of reduction in the outgo 
of food subsidy, enhancing the effi ciency of procurement and PDS and 
encouraging local procurement to the maximum extent thereby extending the 
benefits of MSP to local farmers, the scheme of Decentralized Procurement 
of Foodgrains was introduced by the Government in 1997-98. The scheme is 
now in operation in the States of West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya 
Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu and Uttaranchal. The Union Government 
has been encouraging States to adopt the scheme of Decentralized 
Procurement of Foodgrains. 
The difference between the economic cost of the State Government and the 
Central Issue Prices is passed on to the State Government as subsidy.

Dismantling of PDS 
2246. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it felt in some quarters that Public Distribution System has 
become redundant due to the overflowing granaries of food in the country; 
(b) whether Government are planning to dismantle the Public 
Distribution System; 
(c) whether Govemment are planning to repeal the Essential 
Commodities Act so that the foodgrains can be moved freely from one State 
to the others; 
(d) whether Government are trying to monetise BPL, PDS cards for 
cash, or food stamps instead of grain; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof as to how Government are planning to 
organise the same? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI U. V. 
KRISHNAM RAJU): (a) and (b) No, Sir. 
(c) The Central Government have Issued an Order on 15.2.2002 under 
the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 allowing dealers to freely buy, stock, 
sell, transport, distribute, dispose, acquire, use or consume any quantity in 
respect of wheat, paddy/rice, coarse grains, sugar, edible oilseeds and edible 
oils without requiring any license or permit therefore under any order issued 
under the Act. 
(d) and (e) No, Sir. Questions do not arise.

2249. DR. A.K. PATEL: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, 
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to refer to the reply to 
Unstarred Question 2380 given in the Rajya Sabha on the 8th August, 
2002 and state: 
(a) whether Government have since implemented the steps to minimise 
transit losses such as complete switchover to 50 kgs. (or less) packing and 
improvement in size and quality of jute bags; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government have also procured Non-jute bass such as 
PP/HDPE Woven Sacks of 50 kgs. (or less)  to reduce both cost and losses in 
packing of foodgrains; and 
(d) if so, the quantity thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM 
RAJU); (a) Yes, Sir. With effect from Kharif Marketing Season 2002-2003, the 
Food Corporation of India (FCI) has completely switched over to 50 kg. 
packing norms. With a view to minimize losses during transit due to spillage of 
grains from side seams, the provision of safety union stitch In the jute bags have 
been made by the FCI. 
(b) With a view to further improve the quality of bags and to amend the 
existing Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) of jute bags, certain studies in respect 
of tolerance limit on allowable defects, sampling, criteria for conformity for 
jute bags/fabrics and for fabric faults have been conducted. 
(c) and (d) No, Sir. 
Diversion of foodgrains by FCI 
2250. DR. ALLADI R RAJKUMAR: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the findings of the probe into diversion of wheat meant for the 
consumers to the traders by the Food Corporation of India In Haryana; 
123 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2002] 
(b) the details of the modus operandi of the scandal; 
(c) the quantity and value of wheat diverted to traders, the Monetary loss 
suffered by FCI and the estimated profits made by the traders by selling this 
wheat at exorbitant prices; and 
(d) the action taken against the concerned officials? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUIVIER 
AFFAIRS. FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM 
RAJU): (a) to (d) Food Corporation of India (FCI) sold a total quantity of 29.14 
lakh MT of wheat in the open market at prefixed rates in Haryana during 
October, 1993 to April, 1997. With a view to ensuring that the wheat sold in the 
open market was made available to the local people, the stocks were released to 
traders after obtaining an affidavit from them to the effect that they would not sell 
the stock outside the revenue districts to which they belonged. These traders 
sold the stocks to other parties within the same revenue districts. The buyers of 
wheat through this second sale, who were technically not bound to the affidavit 
given by original buyers, sold the stocks of wheat to parties outside the States. 
The officers of the FCI were suspected to be involved in the above 
diversion of wheat to the open market and the matter was referred to Central 
Bureau of Investigation (CBI) who have completed their investigation in all the 
six cases registered in this behalf. CBI have already filed chargesheet in the 
appropriate Court of Law in two of the cases and closed one case- In the 
remaining three as recommended by CBI, disciplinary action has been 
initiated. However, in one case no action could be taken against an officer who 
had already been dismissed. The FCI did not incur any financial losses on this 
account since wheat under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) was sold 
at rates fixed by the Government from time to time.

Rajasthan and Orissa. 
(b) Shri B.B. Patnaik, Comm ercial Manager (CM), Central 
Warehousing Corporation (CWC), Head Quarter New Delhi & Dr. Ashok 
Kumar, Deputy Director, Storage and Research, Department of Food 
and Public Distribution visited Rajasthan on 22nd & 23rd October,

Shri B.B. Patnaik, CM. CWC, HQ, New Delhi, Shri K.M. Vaghela,

RK. Mahapatra, Senior Regional Manager, and Shri Y.K. Das, Regional 
Manager, Food Corporation of India, Bhubaneswar, Orissa visited Orissa on

(c) The team that visited Rajasthan has reported that the deaths 
in Suvans and Gangapur villages of Baran district could have been

As per the finding of the team that visited Orissa, the alleged deaths in

village o Keonjhar District did not appear to be due to starvation, Adequate

 2265. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: 
DR.T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state; 
(a) whether the rising unsold stocks of sugar and also rising 
sugarcane arrears promised by the respective State Governments 
have resulted in lower sugar prices; 
(b) if so, whether it is feared that around 30 per cent less sugarcane would 
be sown by farmers because of consistent sluggish prices; 
(c) whether this has prompted the farmers to shift to other paying crops; 
and 
(d) if so, what are the concrete remedial measures Government propose 
to take in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE INTHE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION {SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM 
RAJU); (a) to (d) Due to higher level of production during the last four sugar 
seasons, there has been an accumulation of sugar stocks with the sugar 
factories. This has resulted in financial constraints to the sugar factories and 
the consequent increase in cane price dues of the farmers. Further, many mills 
have obtained the orders from the Courts for sale of sugar over and above 
their normal free sale quotas, due to which the prices of sugar have declined 
in the open market. 
So far, no report has been received from any quarter regarding 
reduction in sugarcane area and shifting of sugarcane by the farmers to some 
other cash crops. 
143 

RAJYA  SABHA [12 December, 2002] 
However, the Government has decided to create a buffer stock of 20 
lakh tonnes of sugar for a period of one year. This will enable the sugar mills 
to get a subsidy amount of Rs. 412 crore from the Sugar Development Fund. 
In addition, an amount of Rs. 374 crores would be available from the banks to 
the mills on account of buffer stock. Thus, a total amount of Rs. 786 crores 
would be provided to the mills enabling them to clear the payment of cane price 
dues to the sugarcane growers. This will also help the sugar industry to 
mitigate the financial hardship.

Revamping of public grievances redressal system 
 2313. SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
MISS MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether CVC proposes to revamp the public grievances redressal

PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA 
RAJE): (a) & (b) The Central Vigilanc e Commission (CVC) does not deal 
with public grievances redressal system which is under Cabinet Secretariat 
and Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances. The 
Commission, however, has in place a complaint system for the public to 
lodge complaints relating to corruption of public servants working in Central 
Government Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings, nationalized 
banks, union territories, autonomous organizations like port trusts. The 
complaints can be lodged either electronically through CVC website 
cvc.nic.in or written complaints through mail. 
(c) It has also been the continuing endeavour of the Government to 
check irregularities and malpractices in Government Departments. Policies in 
this regard have been formulated and are continuously monitored and 
modified in order to make them more effective and responsive to the needs of 
the changing environment. The annual Action Plan prepared by the Ministry 
of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions envisages three-pronged 
strategy for containment of corruption in public life. It was initially launched 
in 1985-86 and is 
183 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2002] 
being continued on annual basis. The broad features of the Action Plan are: 
(i)    Preventive vigilance; 
(ii)    Surveillance and detection; and 
(iii)    Deterrent punitive action. 
Steps have also been taken in recent past to make the vigilance 
machinery more effective. These include strengthening the institution of 
Central Vigilance Commission. 
The Freedom of Information Bill 2000 has been passed by the Lok 
Sabha. 
The Lok Pal Bill, 2001 has been introduced in the Lok Sabha on 14 
August, 2001. 
2. Public grievances in the Govenrment of India are redressed through 
decentralized system which functions in every Ministry/ Department. The 
machinery for the redress of public grievances has been strengthened with 
senior officers being designated as Directors of Grievances in every 
Ministry/Department, fixing up time limits for disposal of Public Grievances

(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) and (b) A report on Foreign 
Investhient prepared by a Committee appointed by the Planning Commission 
and submitted to the Prime Minister has proposed some measures to attract 
more FDI into the country which include the following: 
• Consider the enactment of a Foreign Investment Promotion Law that 
incorporates and integrates aspects relevant to promotion of FDI. 
• Urge States to enact a special investment law relating to 
Infrastructure to expedite all investment in infrastructure sectors and 
remove hurdles to production in this critical sector. 
• Empower the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) to give 
initial Central level registration and approvals where possible, with a 
view to speeding up the process of project implementation. 
195 

RAJYA  SABHA [12 December, 2002] 
• Change Government of India's Rules of Business to empower 
Foreign Investment Implementation Authority (FIIA) to expedite the 
processing of administrative and policy approvals. 
• The aggregate FDI target for the Tenth Plan should be disaggregated 
in terms of sectors and relevant administrative 
ministries/departments, to increase accountability. This could help 
ensure that the policy pre-requisites for increasing domestic private 
investment and FDI are expedited by the concerned departments. 
• Sectoral FDI caps should be reduced to the minimum and entry 
barriers eliminated. With the exception of 'Defence Industry*, FDI 
caps can be removed in all manufacturing and mining. Caps can also 
be eliminated in Advertising, Private Banks and Real Estate and 
raised in telecom, Civil Aviation, DTH/KU broadcasting. Insurance 
and Plantations {other than tea). 
• The existing strategy for attracting FDI should be overhauled. The 
relative emphasis must shift from a broad (scatter shot) approach to 
one of targeting specific companies in specific sectors. The Foreign 
Investment Promotion Council (FIPC) should be reformed to 
implement this strategy. It should be chaired by a person with global 
credibility and involve Minister level functionaries w/ho can interact 
with the heads of the Fortune 500 companies. 
• The informational aspects of the strategy should be refined in the 
light of the perceived advantages and disadvantages of India as an 
investment destination and should use information technology and 
modern marketing techniques. 
• the Special Economic Zones should be developed as the most 
competitive destination for export related FDI in the world, by 
simplifying applicable laws, rules and administrative procedures and 
reducing red tape to the levels found in China. The focus should be 
on accelerated/immediate implementation of reforms that may take a 
much longer time [e.g. decade(s)] in the country as a whole and not 
on tax sops. 
• Domestic Policy Reforms in the Power Sector, Urban Infrastructure 
and Real Estate should be expedited to promote private domestic 
and foreign investment.

THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI 
SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA): Madam, the Government has given serious 
consideration to the revival of Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation Limited (HFC) 
and Fertilizer Corporation of India Ltd. (FCI). The complexities relating to the 
revival of these Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) arose on account of 
outdated technologies with serious mismatch in equipment, inherent design 
and equipment deficiencies, intrinsic disadvantages in process technology, 
surplus manpov^rer and huge accumulated losses thereby requiring large 
Investments without any commensurate results in terms of sustained and 
viable operations of the plants. 
In May, 2001, a Group of Ministers was constituted to examine the 
comprehensive rehabilitation proposals in respect of the remaining units of 
HFC and FCI. The recommendations of the GoM were considered by the 
Cabinet on ie.7.2002 and 5.9.2002, and it has been decided to close down the 
entire HFC and FCI, excepting its Jodhpur Mining Organisation. While taking 
this decision, the technology as well as feedstock-related issues, in the context 
of cost of production, the likely impact on the Budget and the availability of 
urea in the country were taken into account, Today, only the gas based units 
are financially and functionally efficient and internationally competitive. 
At the time of closure, none of the units of FCI and HFC was in 
operation. The Haldia Fertilizer Project of HFC, though mechanically 
completed in 1979, could never be commissioned. The operations of Durgapur 
unit have remained suspended since 1997. The operations of Barauni unit of 
HFC, and Ramagundam and Talcher units of FCI have been suspended since 
1999. The Gorakhpur unit of FCI was shut down in 1990. The Sindri unit is 
lying closed since March, 2002. Of the various units of HFC and FCI, only the 
Sindri unit of FCI was in production during 1999-2000 to 2001-02 and even 
this unit produced only 0.76 lakh MT during 2001-02 which is equivalent to 
o.38 % of the urea consumption in the country. Thus the production or non-
product ion of urea by the units of FCI and HFC had no significant impact on 
the availability of fertilizers in the country. 
FCI and HFC have been making losses since inception. Their 
accumulated losses as on 31.3.2002 stood at Rs.7,921 crores and Rs.6.725 
crores respectively. The Government has so far extended Plan/non-Plan 
support including equity to these companies amounting to Rs.3,042.28 crores 
and Rs.2,273.75 crores respectively up to 31.3.2002. For 2002-03, a Budgetary 
provision of Rs.i2i crores from FCI and Rs.87 crores for HFC has been made. 
235 

RAJYA SABHA [12 December, 2002] 
In implementation of the decision of the Govemment -- taken on 
5.9.2002 - to close down the entire HFC and FCI, excepting its Jodhpur Mining 
Organisation, these companies have circuiated the Voluntary Separation 
Scheme (VSS) amongst their employees giving them three months' notice to 
avail the scheme failing vi^ich they will be entitled for retrenchment benefits. 
The scheme of VSS is as per the standing  norms of the Department of Public 
Enterprises. The total number of employees as on 30.9.02 are 4.884 in 
respect of HFC and 5,712 in the case of FCI. The expenditure involved for 
VSS is estimated at Rs.301.25 crores fo r HFC and Rs.390 crores for FCI. In 
the normal course, upon closure of the units, the schools, dispensaries etc. 
should be closed and employees be asked to vacate the company quarters 
forthwith. However, taking into consideration the suggestions of the hon. 
Members of Parliament and related employees associations. FCI and HFC 
have decided to extend the following concessions to their employees after 
their release under VSS: 
Permission to retain company quarters till the end of the current 
academic session (April 2003); 
Continuation of the schools and dispensaries (at reduced scales) till 
the end of the current academic session. 
It is also for information that the country is almost self-sufficient in 
urea. Total availability in 2001-02 was 216 lakh MT (inclusive of 2 lakh MT of 
imported urea) and the consumption has been 199 lakh MT. 
In addition, from the year 2005-06 onwards, 16.52 lakh MT of urea 
from Oman-India Fertilizer Company (OMIFCO) is expected to become 
available which the Government is committed to buy back on a predetermined 
long term fixed price. Further, the expansion projects of KRIBHCO at Hazira 
and RCF at Thai are also under consideration. 
So far as availability of urea in different parts of the country, including 
the eastern region, is concerned, supply is ensured to all the States at uniform 
Statutory Sale Price and no State is allowed to suffer from shortage of 
fertilizers. Based on the above, the decision to close HFC and FCI will have no 
impact on the availability of urea in these States. Government will ensure that 
in future also, fertilizers remain available in the various parts of the country 
adequately at uniform price.
